 Follow Trick-or-treaters can leave the umbrella home this Halloween in CT, but be ready for an autumn chill
 Dan Amarante Mon, October 26, 2026 at 3:52 PM UTC Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Connecticut's little ghosts and goblins may be able to leave the umbrellas at home Saturday. The early Halloween forecast favors dry weather for trick-or-treating, although a late-week cold front could take some of the warmth out of the air before the candy collecting begins.
 Our stretch of quiet weather looks likely to hold through Halloween , giving families an encouraging outlook for an evening outdoors. There is still time for the forecast to change, but rain is not shaping up to be a major concern right now.
 What to expect for Halloween in Connecticut
 Saturday looks mostly sunny, with afternoon temperatures reaching the 60s across much of Connecticut. That should make for a comfortable afternoon for outdoor festivities before readings begin falling after sunset. It's also above normal for this time of year, with an average high temperature in the upper 50s on the final day of October at both inland and shoreline locations.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For trick-or-treaters, an extra layer beneath a costume is a good idea. Temperatures gradually will cool as the evening goes on, so what feels comfortable while getting ready at home may feel a little chilly after a few trips around the neighborhood.
 Temperatures will likely fall through the 50s and into the upper 40s across Connecticut on the evening of Halloween. (Aguacerowx.com)
 Overnight lows are expected to settle into the middle and upper 40s in many communities. Those readings should come later at night, however, rather than when children first head out. The early evening should be milder, and we'll get a clearer picture of temperatures during the busiest trick-or-treating hours as Saturday gets closer.
 The change to watch for
 A cold front is expected to move through around Friday night into Saturday morning, trimming back the warmth that builds late in the week. Friday could reach the lower 70s in parts of Connecticut, but that warmth may not stick around for Halloween.
 The front looks short on moisture, so its main effects should be some clouds, a breeze and cooler air rather than much rain. Its timing and the amount of cooling behind it will help determine how Saturday feels, especially once the sun goes down.
 Advertisement Advertisement For now, outdoor Halloween plans look to be in good shape. Keep an extra layer handy, and check back later this week as the details for Saturday evening come into better focus.
